newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, bonds outperform Euros.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, bonds outperform Euros.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed narrowly mixed, as bonds outperformed Eurodollars in extremely light pre-holiday trade.
March T-bonds clung to gains, which slimmed steadily throughout the day, as the yield curve flattened. Eurodollar futures spent most of the day unchanged.

"I would expect the curve to continue to flatten, especially if payrolls fall as much as I'm expecting," one T-bond futures trader said, adding that he is looking for December nonfarm payrolls to fall about 300,000. He also said year-end demand would support U.S. bonds through the holidays.
Traders' focus on U.S. December employment data, which will be released two weeks from Friday, points to the lackluster tone in U.S. markets ahead of the holidays.

While U.S. personal income and consumption will be released on Monday, most traders were looking at the payrolls data on January 3, as well as U.S. November durable goods data on Friday, December 27, as key indicators.
November income is seen rising 0.6 percent, from unchanged in October, and spending is forecast to increase 0.3 percent, versus October's up 0.5 percent.
However, the data is not expected to spark momentum ahead of the Christmas holidays, most traders said.
Trade will close early for both T-bond and note futures and Eurodollar futures on Tuesday, December 24. CME Eurodollars will close at 1200 CST/1800 GMT, and CBOT bonds will end at 1215 CST/1815 GMT.
Some analysts said good central bank and hedge buying before the auctions this week should keep the upside bias in the marketplace.

"To see hedge funds and central banks back in, when they were selling a few weeks ago, is a compelling reason to respect the market," David Ader, managing analyst at Technical Data, wrote in a newsletter.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were up 05/32 at 113-10/32, June 10-year notes were up 02/32 at 109-21/32, June Eurodollars were steady at 94.32 and June T-bills were also flat at 94.87. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
